source.document: WHO SMART Guidelines — Antenatal Care (DAK L2)

regle_metier: During a cervical exam, if cervical dilation is greater than 2 cm evaluate the possibility of labour

regles.sortie: Measure BP again after 10–15 minutes rest
regles.action: Measure BP again after 10–15 minutes rest
regles.annotation: Given high values (SBP ≥ 140 or DBP ≥ 90) upon first measure, blood pressure should be measured again

regles.sortie: Measure BP again after 10–15 minutes rest
regles.action: Measure BP again after 10–15 minutes rest
regles.annotation: Given high values (SBP ≥ 140 or DBP ≥ 90) upon first measure, blood pressure should be measured again
The health worker should retake the woman's temperature if the first reading is over 38°C
The health worker should retake the woman's pulse rate if the first reading is lower than 60 or higher than 100 beats per minute
If the woman has an abnormal respiratory exam result or respiratory distress, conduct oximetry test

regles.condition: "Respiratory exam result" = "Other abnormal respiratory exam result (specify)"

regles.action: Measure the fetal heart rate again
regles.annotation: Fetal heart rate out of normal range (100–180) – please have the woman lay on her left side for 15 minutes and check again
Cervix is more than 2 cm dilated: check for other signs and symptoms of labour (if GA is 37 weeks or later)
regles.reference: Pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum and newborn care guide (IMPAC) (2015) (1)

regles.annotation: Cervix is more than 2 cm dilated: check for other signs and symptoms of pre-term labour and other related complications (if GA is less than 37 weeks)
regles.reference: Pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum and newborn care guide (IMPAC) (2015) (1)
